subtype: Hands behind the back in respect [Expressing]
passage: I work two desks from Yusuf, so I saw the whole thing. When the regional head walked into our Pune office, Yusuf stopped mid-sentence and stood with his hands clasped behind his back, chin level, listening. I am Reena, and I thought it looked very formal, almost stiff. The regional head asked him about the delivery figures and Yusuf answered clearly, still standing that way. Later in the canteen, Yusuf stood with his hands in his pockets like anyone else, joking with the driver. I cannot tell whether the earlier pose came from respect or nerves. He told me he grew up standing like that before elders at school assemblies.

qa.q: Where did Yusuf stand with his hands behind his back?
qa.a: He stood in the Pune office when the regional head walked in.

qa.q: What did Yusuf's clasped hands most likely show, and what other reading did Reena consider?
qa.a: They most likely showed respect and attentiveness toward the regional head, which he confirmed with his school habit. Reena also wondered if it was nerves, so it could also have been stiffness.

qa.q: What does Yusuf's relaxed stance in the canteen suggest?
qa.a: It suggests the formal pose is tied to setting and the presence of a senior, so it is not his general way of standing.

qa.q: How might the regional head have taken Yusuf's posture?
qa.a: The regional head probably saw it as respectful and attentive, though a person from a more casual office could find it stiff.

grounding: Observer's account of a young professional standing with hands behind the back before a senior as a sign of respect that can seem stiff elsewhere.

subtype: Hands behind the back in respect [Expressing]
passage:
Day 1. Mridul, new at the shipping firm in Rotterdam, met the director and stood with his hands behind his back, as he had before principals at home. The director smiled politely but kept glancing at his posture.

Day 3. Sumit, a Dutch colleague, said, "You stand like a guard. Are you nervous?" Mridul explained that where he grew up this showed respect. Sumit said, "Oh, thank you. Here it can look stiff, but I get it now."

Day 10. Mridul stood with his hands loose and his head slightly tilted while the director spoke, but still gave full attention. The director asked him for his opinion on the schedule.

qa.a: Mridul works at a shipping firm in Rotterdam.

qa.q: Why did Mridul stand with his hands behind his back, and why did the director glance at his posture?
qa.a: He did it as a sign of respect, as he had before principals at home. The director may have read it as stiffness or unease, since it looks different in that office.

qa.q: What did Mridul change by day 10, and what stayed the same?
qa.a: He loosened his hands and tilted his head slightly, but still gave full attention, so his respect was still visible.

qa.q: How might Sumit have first seen Mridul's stance?
qa.a: Sumit first thought Mridul looked like a guard and might be nervous, until Mridul explained the meaning of the pose.

grounding: Illustrates a young professional standing with hands behind the back as respect that may look stiff in another setting, shown over days.
